steps: 01Two droplets approachCloud droplets are liquid water. Their paths bring them together.

steps: 01An existing crystalIce is already present. Hollow rings trace invisible water vapor.
02Vapor adds to iceDeposition changes water directly from gas to solid.
03A larger crystalAdded water builds the ice. Liquid droplets can still coexist nearby.
2d-deposition-guide.text: How ice grows · depositionThree reference frames01An existing crystalIce is already present. Hollow rings trace invisible water vapor.02Vapor adds to iceDeposition changes water directly from gas to solid.03A larger crystalAdded water builds the ice. Liquid droplets can still coexist nearby.Read left to right, or top to bottom. Shapes and timing are illustrative. Below 0°C, some droplets may remain liquid (supercooled).

renderingNote: Only storm-cloud-volume is hidden during 3D interactions to keep software WebGL responsive. Particle geometry, rendering, controls and simulation are active. 2D observations wrap actual Canvas calls; 3D observations read per-render growth metadata and exclude camera-facing orientation. Source instrumentation exists only in the scratch HTTP response.
